key_insight: A 4D CTA pipeline can produce patient-specific ascending aortic strain maps that are reproducible across segmentation sources and preserve low-frequency mechanical patterns well.
engineering_relevance: This enables noninvasive, geometry-aware assessment of aortic wall mechanics that could support risk stratification and clinical decision-making.
method: nnU-Net or observer segmentations were surface-remeshed and deformably registered across 4D CTA phases.
Mesh-based strain was estimated and validated against FE-derived synthetic 4D CT deformations.
Laplace-Beltrami spectral reconstructions were used to test strain reliability across spatial scales.
evidence_signal: Median strain showed minimal bias versus FE reference and narrow limits of agreement across segmentation sources, while 95th-percentile strain was more variable and related inversely to diameter, AHI, and age.
watch_item: Higher-percentile strain metrics are more sensitive to segmentation variability and may require careful standardization before clinical use.
paper_title: Toward Reliable Patient-Specific Aortic Strain Mapping from 4D CTA: Validation, Spectral Structure, and Clinical Potential
